turns.content: I was just diagnosed with MS. I'm 31. I'm still in shock.
A diagnosis like that at 31 is life-altering news. It makes sense that you're in shock. How are you feeling?
Terrified. Angry. Like my future has been stolen. I had plans — a promotion, starting a family. All of that feels impossible now.
The loss of the future you had imagined is a real grief, alongside the medical reality. Do you have support around you?

My partner is trying but I can see him struggling too. I've pushed everyone else away. I don't want to be pitied. I've been having thoughts that maybe dying before it gets bad is better than a slow decline.
Thoughts of dying before the illness progresses — that's something I need to take seriously. How strong are those thoughts?
Strong enough that I've been researching options. I know that sounds extreme for a new diagnosis but I can't get it out of my head.
